title: ضَمَائِرُ الْمَفْعُولِ بِهِ
blocks: Object pronouns make Arabic concise and natural. Instead of repeating a person’s name, Arabic attaches a short ending to the verb.
[callout] Compress the sentence: عَلِيٌّ سَاعَدَهَا. Ali helped her. The ending ـهَا replaces Maryam.
## Use the chapter at the depth you need
- Use two pronoun signals in one word.
هِيَ and the feminine ـتْ identify the subject.
[callout] Powerful Arabic pattern: A single verb may tell you both who performed the action and who received it. In سَاعَدَتْنِي , ـتْ signals “she”, while ـنِي means “me”.

TABLE: Meaning | Ending | Example | Meaning // me | ـنِي | سَاعَدَنِي | he helped me // us | ـنَا | سَاعَدَنَا | he helped us // you — one male | ـكَ | سَاعَدَكَ | he helped you // you — one female | ـكِ | سَاعَدَكِ | he helped you // you two | ـكُمَا | سَاعَدَكُمَا | he helped you two // you — male/mixed plural | ـكُمْ | سَاعَدَكُمْ | he helped you all // you — female plural | ـكُنَّ | سَاعَدَكُنَّ | he helped you all // him / it m. | ـهُ | سَاعَدَهُ | he helped him // her / it f. | ـهَا | سَاعَدَهَا | he helped her // them two | ـهُمَا | سَاعَدَهُمَا | he helped them two // them — male/mixed plural | ـهُمْ | سَاعَدَهُمْ | he helped them // them — female plural | ـهُنَّ | سَاعَدَهُنَّ | he helped them
[callout] Important contrast: possessive “my” is normally ـِي as in كِتَابِي , but verbal “me” is commonly ـنِي as in سَاعَدَنِي .
The verb ending ـتُ shows “I”; ـهُ shows “him”.
[example] قَرَأْتُهُ. I read it — masculine noun.
[example] قَرَأْتُهَا. I read it — feminine noun.
[callout] Non-human reference: use ـهُ or ـهَا according to the grammatical gender of the noun being replaced, not according to biological gender.
## Build a verb with an object ending
### Choose the action and the receiver

[ar] فِي الْأَمْسِ سَاعَدَتْنِي مُعَلِّمَتِي فِي الْمَشْرُوعِ. بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ قَابَلْتُ صَدِيقَيْنِ وَسَأَلْتُهُمَا عَنِ الْعَمَلِ. رَأَيْتُ طَالِبَاتٍ فِي الْمَكْتَبَةِ وَدَعَوْتُهُنَّ إِلَى فَرِيقِنَا. فِي النِّهَايَةِ شَكَرْنَاهُمْ جَمِيعًا.

Yesterday, my teacher helped me with the project. After that, I met two friends and asked them about the work. I saw female students in the library and invited them to our team. At the end, we thanked them all.
Describe a school day, project or helpful experience. Include:
- one form meaning me or us
- one verb that shows both subject and object information
## Write about a school event or helpful experience
Write 7–9 Arabic sentences. Use at least five different object endings and underline them after writing.

[callout] Self-edit checklist: Does each suffix clearly refer to a person or thing already known? Have you distinguished dual, masculine/mixed plural and feminine plural? Does the verb still show the subject correctly?
## Why this grammar matters for confident Arabic communication
Object endings reveal who receives an action, even when the person is not named.
Students must track references such as “him”, “her” and “them” across a text.
Object pronouns reduce repetition and make answers more natural.
They support cohesion, reference and accurate sentence building.

## Common mistakes and how to repair them
Use ـهَا for a feminine singular referent.
Exactly two requires the dual ending.
The verb must show “she”; the object ending must show “me”.
